uncited: It builds on [Real-time transfer function evaluation](1551-real-time-transfer-function-evaluation.md) by providing a mechanism to efficiently select which pre-classified voxels are visible based on the current transfer function configuration.
*   **Input:** A 3D volume dataset with density values; a traversal order (e.g., front-to-back slices); proxy geometry indices corresponding to voxels.
*   **Output:** Pre-loaded iso-value index buffers in graphics hardware (video or AGP memory) and pointers to the start of each iso-value array in main memory.
**Index Buffers:** Arrays of vertex indices for proxy geometry (splat vertices).
*   **When to Use:** When interactive transfer function changes are required.
*   **When Not to Use:** When the transfer function is static, as traditional pre-classification may be slightly faster.

detail: supported

Unlike naive pre-classification which requires rebuilding and reloading the index buffer on every transfer function change (causing CPU-GPU bandwidth bottlenecks), this method uses pre-sorted buffers and pointer merging for interactive rates [S1, unofficial][S2].

The claim accurately reflects the content of the provided evidence. Both Source [S1] and Source [S2] explicitly state that naive pre-classification requires rebuilding and reloading the index buffer on every transfer function change, which causes CPU-GPU bandwidth bottlenecks and prevents interactive rates. They further explain that the proposed method solves this by using pre-sorted buffers (iso-value index buffers) and pointer merging to achieve interactive rates. The specific details regarding the mechanism (bucket sorting, iso-value lists, pointer merging) and the problem being solved (bandwidth bottlenecks) are present in the text.
